data.name: Startup Freak
data.detailed_description:
In Startup Freak you take the role of a budding entrepreneur, and grow your very own software startup from humble beginnings to a multi-million dollar company. Along the way you will have to overcome countless challenges, from building, testing and securing your product, to devising the ideal marketing strategy and securing investment. Through it, you must ask yourself the ultimate question: are you a Startup Freak?

Build a stellar team

Your staff are everything especially in those all-important early years. Hire an awesome team, skilled in technical, design, operational, or sales aspects of your startup.


Build out your product

Create your very own product by researching the market and building bigger and better features that match your users' demands. But building features isn't everything! You must ensure they are tested and bug-free, well secured, and tuned for performance. Features can also be upgraded and enhanced, for example by incorporating responsive design, or adding accessibility.

Plan your infrastructure

Even the best software is worthless without the right hardware to run on. Manage your data centres across the world, by researching better and more powerful servers, and dealing with ever increasing and shifting user traffic to your services.


Find the right sales channels

Not every sales channel is created equal. More importantly, not every sales channel works well for all types of product. It's your job to use data, and a bit of intuition, to figure out the best go-to-market strategy and win against the odds.

Tune your pricing

Pricing software is more art than science. Plan a pricing strategy, test it, and adapt to the market.

On-board investors

Early stage startups are always in dire need of funding. But pitching your venture to a potential investor is no easy feat! Research and understand your would-be investors, put together a convincing slide-deck, and watch them offer you millions for a small share in your company. P.S. don't forget to haggle!

Deck out your office

What startup doesn't want to be the talk of town for its fancy office? Buy all sorts of gadgets and furniture for your office and give your employees yet another reason to stick around.


Make a big exit

Sooner or later, every founder wants to make an exit from their startup and see the fruits of their labours on a check. The number on that check is dependent on every single decision you have made along the way.

reviews.review:
[h1]TL;DR[/h1]
A fun, simple, but not overly casual, turn-based tycoon game with an interesting theme. It still suffers from a somewhat clunky UI, but is stable and very playable for being an Early Access title.

[h1]Pros[/h1][list]
[*]Straightforward and intuitive abstraction of building software.
[*]The game mechanics naturally keep you moving, planning ahead, and expanding.
[*]Exploring the feature landscape via market research, finding powerful requested features.
[*]Interesting take on marketing, and getting investors on board.
[*]Charming art style for 2/3s of the game (see cons)*.
[*]Decent tutorial and a good easy scenario to learn the ropes.[/list]

[h1]Cons[/h1][list]
[*]*The graphics of the program architecture / feature plane are VERY basic.
[*]Lack of accurate “area of effect” forecast for specific software features.
[*]Strong random events that can’t be forecast or mitigated.
[*]A few awkward and clunky UI interactions, but generally quite solid.[/list]

See how it plays here:
https://youtu.be/u2Zq_6zgSUM

[h1]General[/h1]
Yet another software tycoon game? Yeah, it is, but it doesn’t just come with open hands to accept its piece of the oversaturated pie. This one feels quite unique due to how you build your software on a feature plane that is uncovered gradually by market research. Overall I think the game is simple, but not overly casual. 

Your CEO and employees each have four skills that feed all activities you line up for the next turn (“sprint”): building features, security, testing, and performance improvements. You optimize your program for the limited space you have uncovered on the feature plane and try to keep up with improving marketing, branding, server infrastructure, etc. The game leaves you a lot of choice and punishes poor decision making. However, sometimes it just decides to screw you via random events, which can be frustrating because there is little to nothing one can do to avoid the bad effects.

[h1]Game Flow[/h1]
The game flow is one of the game’s strong points. The game mechanics always keep you moving as the customer base expects more and more over time and the competition, albeit invisible, doesn’t sleep. You scale the mountain of ever escalating requests for number of features and program quality, while uncovering new space to accommodate for these features. This also requires an ever more competent team to stay on top, and servers that don’t suffer from Error 37 as soon as your program becomes slightly more popular. This core gameplay loop balances its elements well and just works. It is fun!

[h1]Flaws[/h1]
There is a bit of a dichotomy between the two main screens (HQ and software), where the game throws you back to the HQ which still lacks a lot of information I would like to see, that the software screen does provide.

Most of my criticism lies with the implementation and lack of polish of the software feature building part of the game. It looks very barren in a bad way, has some clunky UI interactions and frustrates when the lack of feature-effect forecasting leaves you with a messed up piece of software through none of your own informed wrongdoing. Once you learn your way around these limitations (or they get fixed as the developer already has hinted at), it plays pretty well overall though!

[h1]State of the Game at Launch[/h1]
The game is rather stable, in 15h+ of gameplay I only had one crash. However, there still are plenty of small and large balancing issues, as well as a general lack of polish. Not more than would be expected of an Early Access title though.

[i]This review is based on the Early Access release version 0.72.[/i]
